text:
rachel: Heads up — after the docusaurus -> mkdocs migration I’m seeing duplicate anchors for a few pages. Build passes but nav anchors jump to the wrong section.

rachel: Example: `guides/installation.md` has frontmatter `title: Install` and also a H2 `## Install` which used to get unique slugs in Docusaurus, but MkDocs now emits the same anchor for both and links to `#install` go to the first occurrence.

tom: That would explain the weird anchor jumps I saw on the QA site. Are the anchors generated from frontmatter titles too? I thought only headings were sluggified.

rachel: MkDocs with `mkdocstrings` and some frontmatter plugins can add heading-like anchors for titles. We added `toc` plugin that also maps page title to a section anchor.

jeff: Quick mitigation: update links to reference page-level anchors (i.e., `/guides/installation/` instead of `#install`) until we canonicalize slugs. But that's a lot of PR churn.

leah: Another option: change mkdocs config to add `use_directory_urls: false` and leave anchors fully qualified (including `.html`) so links are unambiguous. Downside: breaks pretty URLs.

rachel: I prefer not to flip URL structure right now. I prototyped a preprocessor that de-duplicates anchors by appending incremental suffixes when conflicts occur. It rewrites the generated `site` HTML files after build.

tom: Could be OK as an interim, but brittle. Also may confuse external links (permalinks).

rachel: Agreed. Long-term we should normalize how frontmatter titles map to anchors during migration. I can open a migration script to rewrite frontmatter to remove leading duplicates or convert titles to H1 and avoid duplicating H2s.

jeff: For immediate fix in CI: run a headless linkcheck against the built site and surface anchor collisions. I have a small node script that collects `id` attributes and reports duplicates. Want me to add it to the docs CI job?

rachel: Yes please. If the script fails the build (or posts a comment), we can triage high-priority pages first.

ci-bot: New job queued: docs-anchor-check (runs after mkdocs build)

leah: We should also update the docs contributor guide: mention that page titles should not duplicate section headings. Add a linter rule (markdownlint) to catch identical H1/H2 text.

jeff: I'll draft an ESLint-like markdownlint rule and add it to docs package.json. It will run in `pre-merge` CI stage.

rachel: Also found two specific problem pages: `guides/upgrade-v1-to-v2.md` and `api/model-serving.md` where the title and first H2 are identical. I opened small fixes: #3501 and #3502 that adjust headings to be more descriptive.

tom: Thank you — those were the ones QA flagged. After those merges can we re-run linkcheck on the staging renderer?

ci-bot: docs-anchor-check finished: 2 duplicate anchors found (files listed in PR comments).

rachel: Linkcheck output posted on PR #3501. I've merged the H2 tweaks and restarted the staging deploy.

jeff: After the small fixes, the anchor-check job passes locally. I'll push the markdownlint rule and update the CONTRIBUTING checklist.

leah: One more gotcha: some legacy external links use fragment `#install` expecting old Docusaurus slugs. We should keep a redirect map for the first 90 days post-migration.

rachel: Good call. I'll assemble a short redirect mapping (old fragment -> new page URL) and add it to `_redirects` in the hosting config.

jeff: Sounds good. Rolling checklist for followups: 1) add anchor-check CI job (done), 2) add markdownlint rule (in progress), 3) backfill redirects (rachel), 4) long-term migration script to normalize frontmatter (rachel).

rachel: Thanks all — closing this loop once redirects are live. Leaving thread open for any regression reports.

docs-bot: PRs referenced: #3501, #3502. CI: green on staging deploy.

rachel: Deploy looks stable. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
